newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes higher on weather, seedings.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes higher on weather, seedings.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed higher on cold weather in the U.S. winter wheat areas and on spillover support from Friday's bullish USDA winter wheat seedings report, traders said.
"The acreage number was a very low number. Also the cold weather in the Plains is causing concern," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.

Low temperatures the past few days through the nation's mid-section led to concerns about winterkill in wheat but meteorologists said some snow cover should help dampen fears about severe damage to the crop.

"We should see snow in the Central Plains tonight and tomorrow, moving east Wednesday," said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp. "That should provide some protective snow cover for wheat."

But the key behind the gains in wheat futures remained Friday's USDA seedings report. USDA said U.S. farmers last fall seeded 48.222 million acres of winter wheat, well below an average of analysts' estimates for 51.4 million acres.
Wheat closed four to eight cents per bushel higher, with March up four at $3.91. May closed 6-1/4 cents per bushel higher at $3.76-1/4.
